findings.title: 3.2a commit gate cannot pass: tests that assert rendered facts and `Comprehension:` survive until 3.3 and 4.1
findings.description:
3.1 and 3.2 stop rendering `Comprehension:` and the Adoption Facts section while the resolver is still wired in. 3.2a then requires `pnpm --filter @context-forge/core test` to pass. Tests that fail at that point:
- `pipeline-integration.test.ts:154-173` asserts the probe JSON, the WARNING line and `- Squadron: unavailable...`. All three come from the Adoption Facts section.
- `pipeline-integration.test.ts:184` asserts `Comprehension: ${COMPREHENSION}`.
- `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` expects `FACTS_HEADING` in `expectBrownfield` (lines 24 and 99-103).

The first two are deleted in 3.3 and the third in 4.1, both after the 3.2a commit. 3.1's own success check runs only the `SectionBuilder` tests, so it hides the break at `pipeline-integration.test.ts:184`.

Fix: delete the pipeline-integration brownfield block and `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` in 3.1/3.2. Or drop 3.2a and fold 3.1–3.2 into the 3.7 commit.

findings.title: 3.7 `pnpm -r test` fails because `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` is not deleted until 4.1
findings.description:
After 3.3 the signature is `createContextPipeline(projectPath)`. That test still calls `createContextPipeline(dir, { adoptionStateWrites, squadronProbe })` at line 68 and asserts brownfield selection, facts and state writes. It fails at runtime, because vitest does not type-check. 3.3 lists the test files to update but omits this one. 3.7 requires "all four pass" and commits the seam removal.

Fix: move the `adoptionBuild.integration.test.ts` deletion from 4.1 into 3.3.

findings.title: `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` never cover tests, so several success checks verify nothing about test files
findings.description:
All three package `tsconfig.json` files set `include: ["src/**/*"]`, and each `typecheck` script is `tsc --noEmit` on that config. `eslint.config.mjs:9` ignores `**/tests/**`. Affected claims:
- 3.4 "Remove any remaining references in core tests and helpers" has no check at all.
- 3.5 and 3.6 treat typecheck as proof that the tests were updated.
- 4.3 says "any leftover `switch` on `kind` fails to compile". That holds only for `src`.
- 6.1 treats full typecheck and lint as covering test edits.

A stale `adoptionStateWrites` argument or `adoptionFacts` field in a test would pass silently. `tsconfig.test.json` exists for core and mcp-server but is not wired to any script.

Fix: add `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit` for core and mcp-server to 3.4, 3.6 and 6.1. Or add greps over `packages/*/tests` for the removed names. The `cli` package has no test tsconfig, so use greps there.

findings.title: 3.6 skips `generateContext`'s `options` parameter, and one of its steps has nothing to do
findings.description:
3.6 removes `adoptionStateWrites` from `generateContext`. It never says to remove the trailing `options?: ContextToolOptions` parameter (line 69), the `...options` spread at line 100, or the `options` argument both callers pass (lines 214 and 281). Deleting `ContextToolOptions` makes `src` fail to compile, so the gap is found only after the fact.

3.6 also says to "Update its caller in the server setup". `mcp-server/src/index.ts:40` already calls `registerContextTools(server)` with no options, so nothing changes there.

In `integrationSetup.ts`, `createIntegrationClient(options?: ContextToolOptions)` must lose the parameter itself, not only the doc comment. `mcpIntegration.test.ts:50` calls it with no arguments, so it is unaffected.

findings.title: 4.3 "keep the read cases" in `adoptionState.test.ts` drops per-state read coverage
findings.description: The `it.each(ADOPTION_STATES)('round-trips %j')` test at lines 38-41 uses `writeAdoptionState` to seed state, then calls `readAdoptionState`. The test at lines 43-48 is write-only. Deleting both removes the only test that reads each valid state, and `readAdoptionState` stays in use for navigation until 270. The plan should say to rewrite the round-trip test as a read test that seeds TOML with `writeFile`. The remaining tests at lines 34-36 and 50-64 are already read-only and need no change.

findings.title: Commit steps are checkboxes, not `**Commit**:` marker lines
findings.description: 2.3 is a checkbox task, 3.2a is a checkbox task, and the commits in 3.7, 4.1–4.4, 5.1 and 6.3 are `- [ ] Commit:` sub-checkboxes. Markers must be plain `**Commit**:` lines. Convert them and keep them at the working points (after 2.2, after the 3.x seam removal, after each 4.x, after 5.1). With the two FAIL findings fixed, 3.2a probably disappears.

findings.title: 5.1 omits the project registration the MCP calls need
findings.description:
The 5.1 fixture steps list copying the fixture, installing the guide, writing source and adding the comprehension doc. They leave out the step that makes `context_build` and `template_preview` addressable: patching `projects.json` in `fixtureEnv.tempDir` with the checkout path (adoptionParity lines 81-84). The `FIXTURE_PROJECT_ID` is also needed.

The "copy `fixtures/integration-project`" wording is imprecise. The real project root is the nested `tests/fixtures/integration-project/integration-project`, and `projects.json` sits one level above it. The `git show` pointer mitigates this, but the step list should name these.

findings.title: Section 3 intro misstates which package fails to typecheck
findings.description: It says "Between 3.4 and 3.6, only `mcp-server` typecheck is expected to fail." After the 3.4 rebuild, `cli/src/commands/build.ts:84` still passes two arguments until 3.5. So `cli` also fails in that window. The sentence should say "between 3.4 and 3.5 `cli` and `mcp-server` fail, and between 3.5 and 3.6 only `mcp-server` fails".

findings.title: 3.3's services grep also matches a comment and leaves an unused local
findings.description:
- The 3.3 success grep `adoption/\|detection/` over `services/` matches the comment at `ContextIntegrator.ts:9-10` ("never adoption/index.ts… services/ and adoption/"). The comment must be deleted along with the import. The step says only "remove every import".
- After the swap is removed, `const instruction = project.instruction || 'implementation'` (line 148) is unused. `noUnusedLocals` is on in `tsconfig.json`, so the build breaks until it goes.
- Neither is blocking, because the grep and compiler will catch them.

findings.title: Success-criteria coverage and sequencing of D1–D6
findings.description:
Every functional and technical criterion has a task:
- Build writes nothing, reads no state and spawns no `sq`: 3.3, 3.5, 3.6 and the purity test in 5.1.
- Byte identity: 2.1–2.2 capture the golden files before any edit, and 3.7 and 6.1 check them unchanged.
- CLI/MCP parity: 5.1.
- Guide warning kept: 6.1 names two existing tests, and both exist (`cli/tests/commands/build.test.ts:91`, `mcp-server/tests/contextTools.test.ts:162`).
- `services/` imports nothing from `adoption/` or `detection/`: 3.3 and 6.2.
- No orphan exports: 6.2.
- Verification Walkthrough: 6.3.

Deletion order in section 4 is sound:
- 4.1 removes `adoptionCompletion.ts` before 4.3 removes `writeAdoptionState`.
- 4.2 drops the `ProbeOutcome` import from `contracts.ts` before 4.4 deletes `squadronProbe.ts`.

Statements about existing code check out: the `adoption.state` key and the file names, `adoption/index.ts` re-exports (lines 4-6), `detection/index.ts` probe block (lines 7-17), and `adoption-completed` appearing only in `adoptionOutcome.ts` and the resolver (so "if there is none" in 4.3 is correct). No task is scope creep, and no load-test or NFR requirement applies.
